citations.title: Operation of residential facilities
citations.requirement: Apply for the license to the DODD director. DODD does a pre-license survey and gives local officials notice; it cannot issue the license until 10 days (excluding weekends/holidays) after mailing. Initial license ≤1 year, renewal ≤3 years.

citations.title: Prohibiting operation without license
citations.requirement: No one may operate a residential facility, or admit a person with a developmental disability to one, without a DODD license.

citations.title: License not transferable; posting
citations.requirement: License is valid only for the licensee, the named premises, the number of individuals on it, and its term. It is not transferable. Keep it at the facility and show it to anyone on request.

citations.title: Licensee/operator contract
citations.requirement: A licensee may contract with another entity as operator. They need a written agreement requiring the operator to give the licensee the information it needs; the licensee stays responsible for compliance with all rules.

citations.title: HCBS approval and Medicaid provider agreement
citations.requirement: If HCBS is delivered in the facility, submit the DODD application for approval, keep an ODM Medicaid provider agreement, and follow the Chapter 5123-9 rule for each HCBS delivered.

citations.title: Licensee notifications to DODD
citations.requirement: Notify DODD electronically within 14 days of disqualifying-offense charges/convictions, related-party status, a new 5%+ financial interest, or an administrator license suspension; within 7 days of bankruptcy. Keep contact info current.

citations.title: Financial and insurance proof
citations.requirement: At application and on request, show a $10,000 line of credit or a $10,000 daily bank balance for 90 days, plus a general liability certificate of at least $1,000,000 covering individuals' theft/property damage losses.

citations.title: Operator compliance and rights safeguards
citations.requirement: Comply with Chapter 5123-3 and applicable federal, state and local law (ADA, fire code, wage and hour, workers' comp, unemployment, withholding). Safeguard rights under ORC 5123.62 and 5123.65 and meet 5123.63 and 5123.64.

citations.title: Required written policies and procedures
citations.requirement: Written policies are required on person-centered planning, satisfaction, internal monitoring, staff supervision, the training plan, service delivery, background investigations (5123-2-02), and volunteers if used.

citations.title: Internal compliance program
citations.requirement: Show an internal compliance program covering Chapter 5123-3, background investigations, service delivery/documentation/billing, and management of individuals' funds. Take part in DODD data collection when asked.

citations.title: Governing board duties
citations.requirement: A governing board must review annual audit or financial statements, review compliance review reports and plans of correction, monitor the internal compliance program, and promote high-quality services.

citations.title: Background investigations; Rapback; annual abuser-registry notice
citations.requirement: Run 5123-2-02 background checks. The administrator, and a natural-person licensee or operator, must consent to Rapback. Each year give staff written notice of conduct that leads to abuser registry placement and of the 14-day charge-reporting duty.

citations.title: Payroll compliance; staff on duty; support staff
citations.requirement: Stay current on payroll taxes, workers' comp and unemployment premiums. Schedule staff on duty by individuals' needs, with schedules prepared in advance and available at each facility. Provide enough support staff that DSPs are not pulled from primary duties.

citations.title: Personnel records, training plan, training records
citations.requirement: Keep personnel records. Keep a written training plan (competency method; responsible person; timelines) updated at least every 12 months. Record each training's description, date, duration and instructor.

citations.title: Administrator requirements
citations.requirement: Employ an administrator aged 21+ who meets the experience and education tiers. Designate an acting delegate in writing. Notify DODD within 14 days of an administrator change; orientation within 30 days; report if serving more than one licensee.

citations.title: DSP requirements
citations.requirement: DSPs must be 18+ and read/write English. Within 60 days of hire they need Red Cross-equivalent first aid and CPR with in-person skills assessment. Until then they work only with a certified staff present. Appendix B training applies.

citations.title: Supervisor, support staff and direct support assistant requirements
citations.requirement: Supervisors meet the DSP requirements and complete supervisor training within 90 days of becoming a supervisor. Support staff complete appendix C training. Direct support assistants (age 16-17) have limited duties with a DSP.

citations.title: Physical environment standards
citations.requirement: Accessible, clean, safe, homelike. Annual fire inspection; carbon monoxide detector if gas furnace/water heater; 80 sq ft living area per person; max 2 per bedroom (80/120 sq ft); 1:4 bath ratio; free phone access; no signage labeling residents.

citations.title: Fire safety and emergency response plan; equipment
citations.requirement: Have a fire safety and emergency response plan approved by state/local authority and shared with the county board. Post floor plans; keep exits clear; extinguisher on each floor. Facilities with 5 or fewer need smoke detectors on each floor.

citations.title: Fire and tornado drills; training; emergency reports
citations.requirement: Document 3 fire drills per 12 months (morning, afternoon/evening, asleep) and 1 tornado drill. Train each individual within 30 days of residency and yearly. Report any fire with fire department response to DODD within 1 business day.

citations.title: Person-centered planning
citations.requirement: Individuals (or guardians) make decisions about services. For non-ICF homes the county board SSA coordinates assessment and develops the ISP under OAC 5123-4-02; the operator participates and implements the plan.

citations.title: Admission of residents
citations.requirement: Admission is voluntary with informed consent. Admit only those whose needs can be met. Give written admission decision within 30 days of application; notify the county board within 14 days of admitting a resident.

citations.title: Standards of service provision
citations.requirement: Staff provide person-centered services and know the ISP before serving. They take reasonable steps to prevent incidents and follow 5123-2-06. DSPs must not serve their own minor child or spouse, or be impaired by alcohol/drugs on duty.

citations.title: Health care, medication, and disposal
citations.requirement: Medication administration, nurse delegation and medication error reporting follow Chapters 5123-6 and 5123-17. Written disposal procedures need two-staff verification. Medication accounting is due within 24 hours of a death and by the last day of residency on termination.

citations.title: Transportation
citations.requirement: Driver must hold a valid license and liability insurance. Obtain a BMV driving record within 14 days before hire and every 3 years. Drivers with 6+ points are prohibited. Written vehicle accessibility/maintenance/driver policies.

citations.title: Food, clothing and personal belongings
citations.requirement: Offer daily meals and snacks that meet nutritional needs and preferences. Modified/therapeutic diets follow physician or dietitian instructions. Keep 3 days fresh and 5 days staple food. Inventory belongings within 14 days of admission when assessed need.

citations.title: Individuals' service records
citations.requirement: Keep current records at the facility: photograph, legal status, ISP with documented informed consent, and signed authorization to seek medical treatment (or documented attempts). The fetched text was truncated; confirm the remaining items.

citations.title: Transfer and termination grounds and notice
citations.requirement: Initiate transfer/termination only on listed grounds. Give 30 days' written notice by certified mail to the individual and county board, including appeal rights and Disability Rights Ohio contact. Services continue during a hearing unless an emergency exists.

citations.title: Transfer/termination appeal, mediation and hearing
citations.requirement: Appeal to governing board/administrator within 7 days of notice; decision within 5 days; appeal to the DODD director within 5 days. DODD mediation within 15 days, then hearing within 30 days; burden of proof is on the operator.

citations.title: Compliance reviews, summary, appeal and plan of correction
citations.requirement: DODD reviews at least once per license term; special reviews may be unannounced. Summary within 10 days of the review ending. Appeal or plan of correction within 14 days of receipt; DODD acts within 10 days (appeal) or 20 days (plan).

citations.title: License issuance and adverse actions
citations.requirement: Three-year license issued within 20 days of compliance and fee collection; one-year license if adverse action needs a plan of correction. DODD may suspend admissions, place a monitor, or refuse to renew/revoke. Notify residents and guardians within 3 business days.

citations.title: Development and renovation; development approval
citations.requirement: Obtain DODD development approval before applying for a residential facility license. DODD will not approve licensed beds exceeding the statutory limit.

citations.title: MUI: immediate reporting and protective measures
citations.requirement: Employees immediately report suspected or actual major unusual incidents to the provider's designee, the county board, or the DODD hotline. The provider immediately secures medical care and removes staff alleged in physical or sexual abuse from contact.

citations.title: MUI: county board notice and incident report deadlines
citations.requirement: Notify the county board within 4 hours of discovery of abuse, neglect, exploitation, misappropriation, peer-to-peer acts, prohibited sexual relations, unexplained death, or media inquiry. Submit the incident report by 3 p.m. the next working day.

citations.title: MUI categories A, B, C and unusual incidents
citations.requirement: Category A: abuse, neglect, exploitation, death unexplained. Category B: suicide attempt, natural death, medical emergency, missing individual, peer-to-peer, significant injury. Category C: law enforcement, hospitalization, unapproved behavior support.

citations.title: Incident report content
citations.requirement: Incident reports include the individual's name and address, date/time/location, who/what/when/where description, injuries, immediate actions, persons involved, witness statements, notifications, medical follow-up, and the author's signature.

citations.title: MUI scope for round-the-clock services
citations.requirement: For individuals receiving round-the-clock waiver services, all MUIs are reported wherever they occur. Certain types are reported wherever they occur; others only when the individual is being served by the provider.

citations.title: Prohibited measures
citations.requirement: Never use prone restraint, restraint that restricts breathing or causes pain, disabling a communication device, meal denial, dark rooms, painful sound, shock, humiliating treatment, or restrictive measures for punishment or convenience.

citations.title: Restrictive measures: limits
citations.requirement: Chemical/manual/mechanical restraint, rights restriction and time-out are last resort, only for risk of harm (or legal sanction for rights restriction). Time-out: max 30 minutes per incident, 1 hour per 24 hours, never key-locked, constant visual supervision.

citations.title: Behavioral support strategy development
citations.requirement: Use positive measures first. Restrictive measures require documentation positives failed, an assessment within 12 months, a qualified author, informed consent, human rights committee approval, guardian notification terms, and review every 90 days.

citations.title: Chapter 5123-6 definitions: health-related activities and medication errors
citations.requirement: Defines health-related activities (13 listed tasks), delegable nursing tasks, delegating nurse, employer oversight, and medication/treatment error types, including administration by uncertified personnel or without required nursing delegation.

citations.title: HPC provider qualifications
citations.requirement: HPC is delivered only by an independent or agency provider with an ODM Medicaid provider agreement. Licensed providers must keep the 5123.19 license and the Medicaid agreement. Noncompliance may lead to license or certification action.

citations.title: HPC service delivery requirements
citations.requirement: Serve per an ISP under 5123-4-02. No HPC with money management or shared living for the same person. Arrange approved substitute coverage. Use EVV for 15-minute units. Agencies need a documented overtime review process.

citations.title: HPC service documentation
citations.requirement: Document service type, date, place, individual and Medicaid ID, provider and contract number, signature/initials, group size, description tied to the ISP, units or time, and start/stop times.

citations.title: HPC group-size rate adjustments
citations.requirement: One staff serving two individuals: base rate 107% of one-to-one; three individuals 117%; four or more 130%. Rate is divided among those served. Rates by county cost-of-doing-business category.

citations.title: On-site/on-call definition
citations.requirement: On-site/on-call applies only when the individual is expected to be asleep at least 5 continuous hours and the provider is present and available but need not stay awake. It may not be authorized in the provider's own residence.

citations.title: Rights of persons with a developmental disability
citations.requirement: Rights include dignity, privacy, free communication, personal possessions, managing finances by ability, confidentiality of records, grievances without reprisal, freedom from unnecessary restraint, abuse-free living, medical access, and voting.

citations.title: HCBS waivers - shared living
citations.requirement: Shared living is a distinct service: no more than 4 persons with DD in a home where it is delivered; a group of two is paid at 85% of the daily rate. Not combined with HPC for the same individual.

citations.title: Agency provider certification
citations.requirement: Agency providers need a certificate of general liability insurance of at least $1,000,000 and proof of an unencumbered $10,000 line of credit or bank balance for certification.

citations.title: Individual Options waiver
citations.requirement: DODD operates the Individual Options waiver under an interagency agreement with ODM.

citations.title: Background investigations: pre-hire requirements
citations.requirement: Before hire: application, reference attempts, check 7 databases (OIG, abuser registry, nurse aide, sex offender, SAM, ODM exclusion, DRC offender); no hire if listed in (C)(2)(a)-(f). Signed attestation and 14-day charge-notice agreement. Driving record for drivers.

citations.title: Criminal records check, conditional employment, Rapback, 5-year recheck
citations.requirement: Request BCII check (FBI check if not an Ohio resident for 5 years). Conditional employment max 60 days; terminate on day 61 if no result. Enroll DSPs in Rapback within 14 days; recheck databases at least every 5 years.

citations.title: Electronic visit verification (referenced by 5123-9-30(D)(9))
citations.requirement: OAC 5123-9-30(D)(9) requires EVV under this rule for HPC in 15-minute units, except on-site/on-call. Rule text itself not fetched; confirm requirements.

citations.title: Medication/treatment error reporting (referenced by 5123-3-04(E)(4))
citations.requirement: OAC 5123-3-04(E)(4) requires operators to report medication/treatment errors under this rule and 5123-17-02. Rule text not fetched; confirm timelines.

citations.title: Abuser registry (referenced by 5123-3-01(B)(1))
citations.requirement: Defines the abuser registry that operators must check and give staff annual notice about. Rule text not fetched; confirm placement and removal procedures.

citations.title: Individual service plan (referenced by 5123-3-03 and 5123-9-30)
citations.requirement: Governs ISP development and the team for individuals in non-ICF homes and HPC. Rule text not fetched; confirm provider duties and timelines.

citations.title: HCBS settings requirements (federal)
citations.requirement: HCBS waiver settings must be integrated, support choice and rights, privacy, dignity and freedom from coercion; provider-owned residential settings need lease-type protections, visitors, and documented modifications. Text not fetched.

citations.title: Electronic visit verification (federal)
citations.requirement: Federal EVV mandate for Medicaid personal care services. Text not fetched; Ohio implementation per ODM EVV guides.

policies.category: OAC 5123-3-01 (C)(5)(b) Written policies and procedures on management practices
policies.title: Person-Centered Planning, Self-Determination and Community Integration
state_specifics: Individuals (or guardians) make the decisions about their services.
In non-ICF homes the county board SSA coordinates the assessment and develops the ISP (OAC 5123-4-02); the operator participates and implements the plan.
Staff must know the ISP before providing services.
Document the community activities and employment options offered to each individual, as the ISP directs.

policies.category: OAC 5123-3-01 (C)(5)(b) Written policies and procedures on management practices
policies.title: Individual Satisfaction, Internal Monitoring and Evaluation
state_specifics: Collect satisfaction input from each individual at least annually and act on it.
Use internal monitoring to identify and correct service problems.
The governing board reviews compliance review reports and plans of correction.
Participate in DODD data collection when asked.
Trend MUIs, deaths and medication errors for the governing board (internal practice).

policies.category: OAC 5123-3-01 (C)(5)(b) Written policies and procedures on management practices
policies.title: Supervision of Staff
state_specifics: Supervisors of DSPs must meet the DSP requirements.
Supervisors complete supervisor training within 90 days of becoming a supervisor.
Document supervision, including observation of competency and performance.
Staff on duty are scheduled by individuals' needs.

policies.category: OAC 5123-3-01 (C)(5)(b) Written policies and procedures on management practices
policies.title: Service Delivery
state_specifics: Services are person-centered and follow the ISP.
Staff take reasonable steps to prevent MUIs and unusual incidents.
Follow OAC 5123-2-06 for any behavior support strategy.
Where HCBS is delivered, also follow the Chapter 5123-9 rule for that service.

policies.category: OAC 5123-3-01 (C)(5)(b) Written policies and procedures on management practices
policies.title: Background Investigations for Employment
state_specifics: Before hire, check the 7 databases: OIG, abuser registry, nurse aide registry, sex offender registry, SAM, ODM exclusion list and DRC offender search.
Request a BCII check (and an FBI check if the person has not been an Ohio resident for 5 years).
Conditional employment is limited to 60 days; terminate on day 61 if no result has arrived.
Enroll DSPs in Rapback within 14 days; recheck databases at least every 5 years.
Obtain a signed attestation and a 14-day charge-notice agreement; obtain a driving record for drivers.

policies.title: Internal Compliance Program: Chapter 5123-3, Background Investigations, Service Delivery and Billing
state_specifics: Audit the facility against Chapter 5123-3 on a set schedule.
Verify background investigations for the administrator, licensee, operator, DSP supervisors, DSPs, direct support assistants and volunteers.
Reconcile service documentation, schedules and EVV against billing before each claim is submitted.
Report audit findings to the governing board.

policies.title: Management of Individuals' Funds
state_specifics: Individuals manage their own finances to the extent of their ability (ORC 5123.62).
Keep an account transaction record per individual and reconcile it (OAC 5123-2-07, as referenced in 5123-3-04(J)(1)(b)(vii)).
Keep records of negotiable items the individual owns.
At termination of residency, account for and release or dispose of personal funds in the written accounting due within 30 days.
The internal compliance program must review funds management.

policies.title: Safeguarding Individuals' Rights (ORC 5123.62-5123.65)
state_specifics: The operator and all employees interact with individuals in ways that safeguard the rights in ORC 5123.62 and 5123.65.
Meet the requirements of ORC 5123.63 and 5123.64 (confirm statutory text when drafting procedures).
Include the rights in staff orientation and annual training.
Grievances are handled without reprisal.

policies.category: OAC 5123-3-01 (D) Staffing - training plan, personnel records, training records
policies.title: Annual Staff Notice: Abuser Registry Conduct and 14-Day Charge Reporting
state_specifics: Give each staff member written notice every year of the conduct that can lead to abuser registry placement.

Supervisors, DSPs and direct support assistants must report in writing to the operator within 14 calendar days a formal charge, conviction, guilty plea or finding of eligibility for intervention in lieu of conviction.
The offenses are those in ORC 109.572(A)(3)(a)-(e).
Keep a signed acknowledgment in the personnel file.

policies.category: OAC 5123-3-01 (D) Staffing - training plan, personnel records, training records
policies.title: Staff Scheduling and Staff on Duty
state_specifics: Staff on duty are based on the needs of the individuals served, as set out in their ISPs and assessments.
Prepare schedules in advance and keep them available for review at each facility.
The rule sets no numeric ratio or awake-overnight requirement; confirm any ISP-driven requirements with DODD and the county board.
Provide enough support staff that DSPs are not pulled from primary duties.

policies.category: OAC 5123-3-01 (D) Staffing - training plan, personnel records, training records
policies.title: Personnel Records
state_specifics: Keep a personnel record for each employee as the facility's personnel policies require.
Include the application, reference attempts, background investigation results and attestation, training certificates and driving record where applicable.
Keep records confidential and locked.
Federal wage-hour records (29 CFR 516) are also required.

policies.category: OAC 5123-3-01 (D) Staffing - training plan, personnel records, training records
policies.title: Written Training Plan, Competency Methods and Training Records
state_specifics: Plan covers the administrator, DSP supervisors, DSPs, direct support assistants, support staff and volunteers.
Plan must be consistent with individuals' needs, best practice and appendices A-D of OAC 5123-3-01.
State the competency method for each topic (written test, skills demonstration or supervisor observation).
Update the plan at least every 12 months and name who is responsible and the projected completion dates.
Record each training's description, date, duration and instructor name (when applicable).

policies.category: OAC 5123-3-01 (D) Staffing - training plan, personnel records, training records
policies.title: DSP, Supervisor and Support Staff Qualifications; First Aid/CPR
state_specifics: DSPs are 18+ and read and write English.
Within 60 days of hire a DSP needs Red Cross-equivalent first aid and CPR, with an in-person skills assessment.
Until certified, a DSP works only with a certified staff member present.
Supervisors complete supervisor training within 90 days; support staff complete appendix C training.
Pre-service training includes DODD modules, orientation, ISP-specific training and fire safety (per DODD guidance).

policies.category: OAC 5123-3-01 (E) Administrator and delegation of executive authority
policies.title: Administrator Qualifications, Orientation and Responsibilities
state_specifics: Administrator is 21+ with birth certificate, SSN card, photo ID and written English proficiency.
Requires experience in specialized services and in supervision, program oversight and financial management, plus a bachelor's degree or a high school credential with 4 years' experience.
Complete DODD web orientation within 30 days of appointment; consent to Rapback.
Administrator is directly and actively involved in day-to-day operation.
Notify DODD if one administrator serves more than one licensee.

policies.category: OAC 5123-3-01 (E) Administrator and delegation of executive authority
policies.title: Delegation of Executive Authority and Administrator Vacancy
state_specifics: Designate in writing the staff member who holds executive authority during the administrator's temporary absence.
When the administrator leaves, the operator has a plan for identifying a new administrator.
Name the person holding executive authority in the interim.
Notify DODD within 14 days of an administrator change.

policies.category: OAC 5123-3-01 (I)-(J) Direct support assistants and volunteers
policies.title: Direct Support Assistants (Age 16-17)
state_specifics: Direct support assistants work only with a DSP and have limited duties.
They never provide intimate personal care and never drive to transport an individual.
They never administer medication or perform health-related activities.
They never do any task the individual forbids and never implement any restrictive measure under OAC 5123-2-06.
Child-labor hour limits for minors (29 CFR 570) also apply.

policies.category: OAC 5123-3-01 (I)-(J) Direct support assistants and volunteers
policies.title: Volunteers
state_specifics: Volunteers are supervised by paid supervisory staff at all times.
Volunteers never provide intimate personal care, administer medication or perform health-related activities.
A volunteer giving more than 40 hours of direct service per calendar year completes appendix D training and a background investigation at least every 5 years.
Do not engage a volunteer who is on a listed database or has a disqualifying conviction within the exclusionary period.
Use this policy only if the facility uses volunteers.

policies.category: OAC 5123-3-02 (F) Fire safety and emergency response plan
policies.title: Fire Safety and Emergency Response Plan: Approval, Content and Posted Floor Plans
state_specifics: The plan is approved by the state or local authority and covers fire, tornado and other natural disaster.
Include a smoking and combustible-storage policy and a fire safety training program covering rescue, alarm, containment and evacuation.
Share the plan with the county board of DD.
Post a graphic floor plan unobstructed on each floor showing exits, pull stations, fire escapes, the 911/fire department number, tornado shelter and meeting places.
Keep an extinguisher on each floor; smoke detectors on each floor in facilities of 5 or fewer.

policies.category: OAC 5123-3-02 (F) Fire safety and emergency response plan
policies.title: Tornado Shelter, Weather/Disaster Response, Evacuation and Re-Entry
state_specifics: Designate a tornado shelter or safe area and the procedure for reaching it.
Write the responses to fires, weather emergencies and disasters when relocation is not required.
Write the responses when relocation is required, including a pre-arranged meeting place.
Write a procedure for permitting re-entry after a drill or physical evacuation.

policies.category: OAC 5123-3-02 (F) Fire safety and emergency response plan
policies.title: Fire Safety and Tornado Drills and Emergency Training
state_specifics: Conduct and document at least 3 fire drills per 12 months: morning, afternoon/evening and while individuals are asleep.
Conduct and document at least 1 tornado drill per 12 months.
Drills may be announced or unannounced and follow assessed needs in the ISP.
Staff are trained in fire safety, equipment and warning systems, and the plan.
Each individual is trained within 30 days of residency and at least every 12 months.

policies.category: OAC 5123-3-02 (F) Fire safety and emergency response plan
policies.title: Emergency Reporting and Relocation Notifications
state_specifics: Report to DODD within 1 business day any fire to which a local fire department responded.
Notify each individual's family member or guardian as soon as possible when an emergency requires relocation.
Report to DODD and the county department of job and family services within 1 business day when relocating individuals.
Give DODD weekly updates on relocated individuals until they return or permanently relocate.

policies.title: Admission of Residents, Informed Consent and County Board Notification
state_specifics: Admission is voluntary and requires informed consent.
Admit only individuals whose service needs the facility can meet; consider the ability to keep adequate services for all residents.
Give the individual and the referring party a written admission decision within 30 calendar days of receiving the application and referral information.
After securing informed consent, notify the county board in writing within 14 calendar days of admitting a new resident.
Never exceed the licensed capacity (ORC 5123.20; OAC 5123-3-01(C)(1)).

policies.title: Standards of Service Provision and DSP Restrictions
state_specifics: The operator, administrator and staff provide person-centered services, communicate effectively with each individual and know the ISP before serving.
Take all reasonable steps to prevent MUIs and unusual incidents; comply with OAC 5123-2-06.
A DSP may not serve the DSP's minor child or spouse, or the administrator's minor child or spouse.
A DSP may not administer medication or perform health-related activities unless qualified under Chapters 4723., 5123. and 5126. of the Revised Code.
No DSP may use or be under the influence of alcohol, illegal or controlled substances that affect service.

policies.title: Self-Administration of Medication and Delegated Nursing Tasks
state_specifics: Self-administration and assistance with it follow OAC 5123:2-6-02.
Delegation of nursing tasks (excluding health-related activities) follows OAC 5123-6-06 and Chapter 4723-13.
Chapter 5123-6 defines the 13 health-related activities and delegable nursing tasks.
Document the delegating nurse and the employer oversight for each delegation.

policies.title: Medication Administration by Certified Staff and Error Reporting
state_specifics: Administer prescribed medication under ORC 5123.42-5123.46 and Chapters 5123-6 and 5123:2-6.
Administration by uncertified staff, or without required nursing delegation, is a reportable error.
Report medication and treatment errors under OAC 5123-6-07 and 5123-17-02; confirm the OAC 5123-6-07 timelines before finalizing.
Keep medication and treatment records showing the prescriber and the date, time and person who administered.

policies.title: Medication Disposal and Accounting at Termination or Death
state_specifics: Disposal of prescribed medication is verified and recorded by two staff members or an independent external entity.
Dangerous drugs are disposed of under OAC 4729-9-06.
On termination: complete a written accounting by the last day of residency, verified by two staff, and plan the transfer of medication to the individual or guardian.
On death: complete the accounting immediately and no later than 24 hours after, verified by two staff.
Cooperate with any investigation; delay disposal if an investigation requires it.

policies.title: Nursing Oversight, Health Monitoring, Change of Condition and Emergency Medical Care
state_specifics: Keep a signed authorization to seek medical treatment, or document attempts to obtain one.
Staff immediately secure medical care in an emergency; medical emergencies are Category B MUIs.
Seizure, choking-risk and health-monitoring procedures follow each individual's ISP and clinical orders.
No Ohio rule prescribing a nursing level was located; the nurse consultant role is the operator's choice.
Notify the guardian and the county board of significant changes.

policies.title: Death of an Individual
state_specifics: Notify the county board within 4 hours of discovery of an unexplained death.
Natural death is a Category B MUI; unexplained death is Category A.
Submit the incident report by 3 p.m. the next working day.
Complete the medication accounting within 24 hours, with two staff verifying.
Cooperate with law enforcement and any legally authorized investigation.

policies.title: Transportation and Vehicle Safety
state_specifics: Provide or arrange transportation per each resident's ISP.
Each driver holds a valid license and valid personal or corporate liability insurance as Ohio law specifies.
Obtain a BMV driving record no earlier than 14 days before initial employment as a driver and at least every 3 years; 6 or more points bars driving.
Drivers must notify the operator in writing immediately of 6 or more points or a suspended or revoked license.
Write policies on vehicle accessibility, maintenance and driver requirements.

policies.title: Food, Meals, Nutrition and Modified Diets
state_specifics: Offer daily meals and snacks that meet nutritional needs and the individual's preferences.
Modified-texture or therapeutic diets follow a physician's or licensed dietitian's written instructions, kept in the record.
Provide variety and substitutions, accommodate religious beliefs, and let individuals take part in meal planning and preparation.
Keep fresh food for 3 days and staple food for at least 5 days at all times.
Prepare and store food per health codes, away from cleaning and laundry compounds.

policies.title: Clothing and Personal Belongings
state_specifics: Each individual has adequate, well-fitting clothing in good repair, comparable in style to that of age peers; encourage independent selection and care.
If assessed to need help with possessions, inventory clothing and belongings within 14 days of admission and update at least annually.
Add any item with a purchase price of $50 or more when acquired and delete it when discarded or lost.
Never discard belongings without the consent of the individual or guardian.
Convey clothing and belongings to the incoming operator if operation is transferred.

policies.category: OAC 5123-3-04 (J) Individuals' service records, confidentiality and retention
policies.title: Individuals' Service Records
state_specifics: At the facility, keep current: photograph, legal status, ISP with informed consent, medical treatment authorization, and medication/treatment records.

Keep accessible and provide to DODD on request: former versions, admission and referral records, service documentation, medical, dental and immunization records, and MUI records and investigation files.
Also keep account reconciliations, negotiable-item records and clothing/belongings records.
Within 30 days after termination of residency, complete a written accounting (circumstances, new address, records, medications, belongings, funds).

policies.category: OAC 5123-3-04 (J) Individuals' service records, confidentiality and retention
policies.title: Confidentiality, Privacy and HIPAA
state_specifics: All information in an individual's record is confidential.
Protect records from unauthorized disclosure, whether paper or electronic.
Confidentiality of records is also a right under ORC 5123.62.
Train staff at orientation; designate a privacy officer.
Release records only with authorization or as law permits.

policies.category: OAC 5123-3-04 (J) Individuals' service records, confidentiality and retention
policies.title: Records Retention and Transfer of Facility Operation
state_specifics: Develop a written retention schedule that meets applicable state and federal requirements.
Confirm the Medicaid retention period with ODM/DODD before finalizing the schedule.
HIPAA privacy documentation is retained for 6 years.
If operation transfers to another operator, convey the records in (J)(1) to the incoming operator.

policies.category: OAC 5123-3-05 (C)-(G) Transfer and termination of services policies
policies.title: Grounds for Transfer or Termination and Nondiscrimination
state_specifics: Allow each resident to remain; initiate transfer or termination only on a listed ground.

Grounds: the resident's welfare and needs can no longer be met without undue hardship; the resident no longer needs or wants services or chooses to move; significant risk of substantial harm to self, others or staff; nonpayment (including Medicaid or other third party); permanent capacity reduction; or the facility ceases to operate.
Never discriminate on disability, race, color, religion, national origin or ancestry, sex or age.
Make reasonable accommodations for physical, mental or behavioral support needs unless undue hardship.

policies.category: OAC 5123-3-05 (C)-(G) Transfer and termination of services policies
policies.title: Notice of Transfer or Termination
state_specifics: Give the individual and the county board written notice by certified mail.

Notice states the reason, effective date, a summary of efforts to meet the person's needs (including work with the county board), appeal rights and process, and the telephone number and address of Disability Rights Ohio.
Explain the notice and appeal rights in a way the individual understands, and record the reasons in the record.
Give at least 30 calendar days' notice, except in an emergency (the individual may return if the emergency ends before the 30 days expire).
If a hearing is requested, maintain services until a decision, unless an emergency exists or the person waives appeal rights in writing.

policies.category: OAC 5123-3-05 (C)-(G) Transfer and termination of services policies
policies.title: Appeal, Mediation and Hearing Process
state_specifics: Appeal in writing to the governing board or administrator within 7 days of receipt; the board or administrator answers in writing within 5 days by certified mail; the individual has 5 days to appeal to the DODD director.
Mediation is held within 15 days of the appeal, with a DODD mediator; no legal representation; non-binding unless all agree in writing; statements are not admissible later.
The DODD-appointed hearing officer (not the mediator) holds the hearing within 30 days after mediation ends; burden of proof is on the operator.
The hearing officer issues a recommendation within 10 days; the director decides within 5 days and may impose conditions.
Failure to follow this rule or the director's decision can lead to adverse action under OAC 5123-3-06.

policies.title: Organization, Governing Body, Operator Duties and Policy Review
state_specifics: If a separate operator is contracted, require a written agreement obliging it to give the licensee needed information; the licensee remains responsible for compliance.
The governing board reviews annual audit or financial statements and compliance review reports and plans of correction, monitors the internal compliance program and promotes high-quality services.
Comply with ADA, fire code, wage and hour, workers' compensation, unemployment and withholding rules.
Review the policy manual at least annually and after rule changes; keep version history.

policies.title: Licensure, Licensed Capacity, Development Approval and Renewal
state_specifics: Obtain DODD development approval (OAC 5123-3-08) before applying; apply to the DODD director.
DODD conducts a pre-license survey and gives local officials notice; no license is issued until 10 days (excluding weekends and holidays) after mailing.
Initial license runs no longer than 1 year; renewals no longer than 3 years; the 3-year license issues within 20 days of compliance and fee collection.
The license is valid only for the licensee, premises, named capacity and term; it is not transferable, and the original is kept at the facility.

Fees per the LSC table (as of 1/31/2025): $100 initial and $300 three-year for 15 or fewer beds; confirm current amounts. Bed-limit rules conflict across sources: confirm the controlling cap with DODD.

policies.title: Required Reports and Notifications to the State; Financial and Insurance Proof
state_specifics: Notify DODD electronically within 14 days of disqualifying-offense charges or convictions, related-party status, a new 5%+ financial interest, or an administrator license suspension, and within 7 days of bankruptcy.
Report an administrator change within 14 days.

Maintain a $10,000 line of credit or $10,000 daily bank balance for 90 days, and general liability insurance of at least $1,000,000 including individuals' theft and property-damage losses; produce proof on request.
Keep a calendar and tracker for fire reports (1 business day), MUI notices (4 hours) and incident reports (3 p.m. next working day).

policies.title: Compliance Reviews, Plans of Correction and Adverse Action
state_specifics: DODD reviews at least once per license term; special reviews may be unannounced.
DODD issues a written summary within 10 days of the review ending.
Appeal or submit a plan of correction within 14 days of receipt; DODD acts within 10 days (appeal) or 20 days (plan).
Adverse actions include suspension of admissions, a monitor, refusal to renew or revocation.
Notify residents and guardians within 3 business days of an adverse action.

policies.title: Individual Rights, HCBS Settings Requirements, Informed Consent and Communication Access
state_specifics: ORC 5123.62 rights include dignity, privacy, free communication, personal possessions, voting, medical access and freedom from abuse and unnecessary restraint.
Free telephone access; no signage labeling residents.
The setting supports choice, privacy, dignity and community integration; any modification is individually justified and documented.
Obtain and document informed consent and support decision-making; provide language and communication access (interpreters, accessible formats) at no charge.

policies.title: Rights Restrictions and Due Process
state_specifics: A rights restriction is a last resort, only for risk of harm (or legal sanction), and only with documentation that positive measures failed.
Requires assessment within 12 months, a qualified author, informed consent and human rights committee approval.
Review at least every 90 days; notify the guardian as the rule requires.
Never use a restriction for punishment or staff convenience.

policies.title: Grievances and Complaints
state_specifics: Individuals may file grievances without reprisal (ORC 5123.62).
Give the grievance procedure at admission, in a form the person understands.
Record each grievance, the response and the resolution; the governing board reviews trends.
Disability Rights Ohio contact information appears in notices of transfer or termination.
DODD contact on the research file: 1-800-617-6733.

policies.title: Personal Funds and Property Management
state_specifics: Individuals control their own funds to the extent of their ability.
Keep each individual's funds separate from operating funds; keep a transaction ledger and reconcile it (OAC 5123-2-07, as referenced).
The 2026 SSI federal benefit rate is $994 per month; confirm any room-and-board charge in writing with DODD and the county board before collecting.
Inventory belongings and negotiable items as OAC 5123-3-04(H) and (J) require.

policies.title: Medicaid Provider Agreement, HCBS Approval and Service Boundaries (HPC and Shared Living)
state_specifics: If HCBS is delivered in the facility, submit the DODD application, keep an ODM Medicaid provider agreement and follow the Chapter 5123-9 rule for each service.
Licensed providers must keep the ORC 5123.19 license and the Medicaid agreement.
Never provide HPC and money management or shared living to the same individual.
Shared living: no more than 4 persons with DD per home; group of two paid at 85% of the daily rate.
ODM enrollment moratorium 5/14/2026-11/14/2026 per ODM notice; confirm applicability with ODM.

policies.title: HPC Service Delivery, ISP Implementation and Documentation
state_specifics: Deliver HPC per the ISP (OAC 5123-4-02) and arrange approved substitute coverage.
Documentation: service type, date, place, individual and Medicaid ID, provider and contract number, signature or initials, group size, ISP-linked description, units or time, and start/stop times.
On-site/on-call applies only if the individual is expected to sleep at least 5 continuous hours and the provider need not stay awake; not authorizable in the provider's own residence.
Agencies need a documented overtime review process.

policies.title: EVV, Billing and Rate Rules
state_specifics: EVV is required for HPC billed in 15-minute units, except on-site/on-call; claims must match an EVV visit; ODM provides Sandata at no cost.
HPC is billed in 15-minute units, up to 16 hours (64 units) per day by assessed need; submit claims within 350 days of service.
Group-size rates: 107% of the one-to-one rate for two individuals, 117% for three, 130% for four or more, divided among those served.
Rates follow the county cost-of-doing-business category; use the current appendix B table.
Confirm EVV requirements (OAC 5160-1-40) and any SB 315 GPS rule changes before finalizing.

policies.title: Positive Behavior Support and Restrictive Interventions
state_specifics: Use positive measures first.
Prohibited: prone restraint, restraint that restricts breathing or causes pain, disabling a communication device, meal denial, dark rooms, painful sound, shock and humiliating treatment.
Chemical, manual and mechanical restraint and time-out are last resorts, only for risk of harm.
Time-out: maximum 30 minutes per incident and 1 hour per 24 hours; never key-locked; constant visual supervision.
Unapproved behavior support is a Category C MUI; review strategies every 90 days.

policies.title: Abuse, Neglect and Exploitation Prevention and Reporting
state_specifics: Employees immediately report suspected or actual MUIs to the designee, the county board or the DODD hotline.
Immediately secure medical care and remove staff alleged in physical or sexual abuse from contact with individuals.
Notify the county board within 4 hours of abuse, neglect, exploitation or misappropriation.
Check the abuser registry (OAC 5123-17-03) and give staff the annual notice.
Prohibit retaliation against reporters.

policies.title: Reportable Incidents, Investigations and Missing Person/Elopement
state_specifics: Category A: abuse, neglect, exploitation, unexplained death. Category B: suicide attempt, natural death, medical emergency, missing individual, peer-to-peer act, significant injury. Category C: law enforcement involvement, hospitalization, unapproved behavior support.
Notify the county board within 4 hours for listed types; submit the incident report by 3 p.m. the next working day.
Incident reports include name, address, date, time, location, description, injuries, actions, persons involved, witness statements, notifications, follow-up and author signature.
For round-the-clock waiver services, report all MUIs wherever they occur.
Write a missing-person response (search, 911, notifications) and report it as a Category B MUI.

policies.title: Residential Environment and Accessibility
state_specifics: The home is accessible, clean, safe and homelike.
Annual fire inspection; carbon monoxide detector if a gas furnace or water heater.
At least 80 sq ft of living area per person; no more than 2 per bedroom (80 sq ft single, 120 sq ft double); 1 bathroom per 4 individuals.
Free telephone access; no signage labeling residents.
Confirm local zoning, building and occupancy approvals.

policies.title: Infection Prevention, Employee Health and TB Screening
state_specifics: Keep an OSHA bloodborne pathogens exposure control plan, offer hepatitis B vaccine, and train staff.
No Ohio rule specifying TB screening for staff was retrieved; adopt a screening procedure and confirm DODD expectations.
Standard precautions, hand hygiene, cleaning and laundry procedures.
Exclude ill staff per written criteria.
Document employee health records in a confidential file apart from the personnel file.

policies.title: Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries
state_specifics: No staff impairment by alcohol or drugs while on duty.
DSPs may not serve their own minor child or spouse, or the administrator's minor child or spouse.
Prohibit financial exploitation, borrowing, personal gifts and unreported prohibited sexual relations (an MUI category).
A related guardian may be paid staff only after approval of the probate court (per DODD).
Staff sign a code of conduct at hire and annually.

policies.title: Wage and Hour, Payroll and Overtime Compliance
state_specifics: Stay current on payroll taxes, workers' compensation and unemployment premiums.
Ohio minimum wage 2026 is $11.00 per hour for covered employers (employers grossing under $405,000 follow the federal minimum); confirm on the Ohio poster.
Overtime at 1.5 times after 40 hours per week; federal FLSA may apply even where the state rule does not.
Agency providers keep a documented overtime review process (OAC 5123-9-30(D)).

documents.title: Licensed residential facilities - administration and operation
documents.how_used: Primary source. Paragraph (C)(5)(b) lists the written policies and procedures an operator must have. Paragraph (C)(5)(c) lists the internal compliance program. Paragraph (D) covers the training plan and personnel policies.

documents.title: Licensed residential facilities - physical environment standards, fire safety, and emergency response planning
documents.how_used: Source for the required fire safety and emergency response plan, drills, training and reporting (paragraph (F)). Physical plant standards in this rule are excluded because they are not policy content.

documents.title: Licensed residential facilities - admission of residents, provision of services, and maintenance of service records
documents.version: Effective 12/1/2022; five-year review 12/1/2027. The text was read from the Cornell LII copy of the Ohio rule.
documents.how_used: Source for admission, medication disposal, transportation, food, clothing and personal belongings, and records and confidentiality requirements. Items that expressly require written procedures or policies are marked 'written'.

documents.title: Licensed residential facilities - transfer and termination of services
documents.how_used: Source for the uniform transfer/termination (discharge) policies, notice and appeal process. Paragraph (C) is titled 'Transfer and termination of services policies'.

documents.title: Residential Facility Development Application (with checklist)
documents.how_used: Context only. I saw only a search excerpt of this application checklist, and it appears to list inspections and application paperwork, not policy content. No items were taken from it.

required_items.text: Written policies and procedures that address management practices regarding: Person-centered planning and self-determination;
Individuals' satisfaction with services delivered;
Internal monitoring and evaluation procedures to improve services delivered;
Supervision of staff;
The training plan described in paragraph (D)(7) of this rule;
Service delivery;
Background investigations for employment in accordance with rule 5123-2-02 of the Administrative Code; and
Volunteers (when the residential facility engages volunteers).
Demonstrate an established internal compliance program to ensure compliance with requirements for: Residential facilities in accordance with rules in Chapter 5123-3 of the Administrative Code;

Background investigations and appropriate actions in accordance with rule 5123-2-02 of the Administrative Code, for its administrator, licensee, operator, supervisors of direct support professionals, direct support professionals, direct support assistants, and volunteers;

Service delivery, service documentation, and billing for services in accordance with Chapter 5123. of the Revised Code and rules adopted pursuant to that chapter for supported living services and the specific home and community-based services provided; and
Management of individuals' funds.
Ensure the operator and its employees interact with individuals in a way to safeguard the rights of individuals enumerated in sections 5123.62 and 5123.65 of the Revised Code.
Meet the requirements established under sections 5123.63 and 5123.64 of the Revised Code.

Annually notify in writing each of its staff members explaining the conduct for which the staff member may be placed on the abuser registry, and set forth the requirement for supervisors of direct support professionals, direct support professionals and direct support assistants to report in writing to the operator, within fourteen calendar days, a formal charge, conviction, guilty plea, or finding of eligibility for intervention in lieu of conviction for the offenses listed in divisions (A)(3)(a) to (A)(3)(e) of section 109.572 of the Revised Code.
Ensure that staff are on duty on the basis of the needs of individuals being served. Staff schedules will be prepared in advance and available for review at each residential facility.
Maintain personnel records for each employee in accordance with the residential facility's personnel policies.

Develop and implement a written training plan for its administrator, supervisors of direct support professionals, direct support professionals, direct support assistants, support staff, and volunteers that:
Is consistent with the needs of individuals served, best practice, and the requirements set forth in appendix A, appendix B, appendix C, and appendix D to this rule.
Describes the method (e.g., written test, skills demonstration, or documented observation by supervisor) that will be used to establish competency in areas of training.
Is updated at least once every twelve months and identifies who is responsible for arranging or providing the training and projected timelines for completion of the training.

Maintain a written record of training completed by the administrator, supervisors of direct support professionals, direct support professionals, direct support assistants, support staff, and volunteers that includes a description of the training completed, the date of training, the duration of training, and when applicable, the instructor's name.
An operator will designate in writing a staff member to whom executive authority has been delegated in the temporary absence of the administrator.

When the administrator leaves a residential facility's employ, the operator will provide the operator's plan for identifying a new administrator and identify the person to whom executive authority has been delegated in the interim period.

A person employed as a direct support assistant will not, under any circumstances: (a) provide intimate personal care; (b) operate a vehicle to transport an individual; (c) administer medication or perform health-related activities; (d) provide any care or perform any task expressly forbidden by the individual; or (e) implement any restrictive measure as defined in rule 5123-2-06.

Volunteer requirements (applies when the facility uses volunteers): volunteers are under supervision of paid supervisory staff at all times; volunteers do not provide intimate personal care, administer medication, or perform health-related activities; volunteers who provide more than forty hours of direct service per calendar year complete appendix D training and a background investigation at least once every five years; and the operator will not engage a volunteer who is on the listed databases or who has a disqualifying conviction within the exclusionary period.

Each residential facility will have a fire safety and emergency response plan approved by the state/local authority that at a minimum, addresses the actions to be taken in the event of a fire, tornado, or other natural disaster.
A policy that addresses smoking regulations and the storage of combustible materials;
A fire safety training program that includes provisions for rescue, alarm, containment, and evacuation;
Designation of a tornado shelter or safe area in the residential facility and the procedure for accessing the area;
Responses to fires, weather-related emergencies, or other disasters when relocation of individuals is not required;

Responses to fires, weather-related emergencies, or other disasters when relocation of individuals is required, including designation of a pre-arranged place to meet in case of a physical evacuation of the residential facility; and
A procedure for permitting re-entry to the residential facility following a fire safety drill and/or physical evacuation.
The residential facility will share the fire safety and emergency response plan with the county board of developmental disabilities.

A current graphic floor plan will be posted unobstructed on each floor and in an area most appropriate for the posting of staff information, including: (a) primary and secondary means of exit from each floor; (b) location of pull stations and fire control system panels, when applicable; (c) fire escapes; (d) telephone number of the local fire department or 911; (e) designated tornado shelter or safe area; and (f) designated meeting places in case of fire.

The operator shall conduct and document at least three fire safety drills in a twelve-month period with one conducted during the morning, one conducted during the afternoon or evening, and one conducted during the time when individuals are routinely asleep.
The operator shall conduct and document at least one tornado drill in a twelve-month period.
Fire safety drills and tornado drills may be announced or unannounced and will be conducted in accordance with the assessed needs of individuals as identified in their individual service plans.

Residential facility staff will be trained in fire safety, operation of fire safety equipment and warning systems, and the residential facility's fire safety and emergency response plan in accordance with rule 5123-3-01.

Each individual will participate in documented training of the fire safety and emergency response plan within thirty calendar days of residency and at least once during every twelve-month period thereafter, appropriate to the individual's needs based on assessment.

Except at an ICF/IID, individuals may be trained to assist one another in case of fire or other emergency to the extent their abilities permit without additional personal risk and as indicated in their individual service plans.
Report to the department within one business day any fire to which a local fire department responded.
Notify each individual's family member or guardian, as applicable, as soon as possible when an emergency requires the operator to relocate individuals from the residential facility.
Report to the department and the county department of job and family services within one business day when an emergency requires the operator to relocate individuals.
Provide weekly updates to the department about individuals who have been relocated due to an emergency until the individuals return or permanently relocate.

Admission of residents - an operator shall: (a) admit as residents only individuals whose service needs can be met by the residential facility; (b) when reviewing an application for admission, consider its ability to maintain adequate services to all residents; (c) notify the individual and referring party in writing of the admission decision within thirty calendar days of receiving an application and referral information; (d) notify the county board in writing within fourteen calendar days of admitting a new resident, after securing informed consent to provide the notification. (C)(1): Admission to a residential facility is voluntary, requiring informed consent.

Standards of service provision - the operator, administrator, and staff shall: (a) provide services in a person-centered manner; (b) be able to effectively communicate with each individual; (c) be knowledgeable in the individual service plan before providing services; (d) implement services in accordance with the individual service plan; (e) take all reasonable steps to prevent the occurrence or recurrence of major unusual incidents and unusual incidents; (f) comply with rule 5123-2-06 regarding behavioral support strategies.

An operator shall ensure that a direct support professional does not: (a) provide services to the DSP's minor child; (b) provide services to the DSP's spouse; (c) provide services to the minor child of the administrator; (d) provide services to the spouse of the administrator; (e) administer medication or perform health-related activities unless the DSP meets the applicable requirements of Chapters 4723., 5123., and 5126. of the Revised Code; (f) use or be under the influence of alcohol, illegal drugs, illegal chemical substances, or controlled substances that may adversely affect the ability to furnish services while providing services.
Self-administration or assistance with self-administration of prescribed medication will be conducted in accordance with rule 5123:2-6-02 of the Administrative Code.
Delegation of nursing tasks, excluding the provision of health-related activities, will be conducted in accordance with rule 5123-6-06 and Chapter 4723-13 of the Administrative Code.
Administration of prescribed medication pursuant to sections 5123.42 to 5123.46 of the Revised Code will be conducted in accordance with Chapters 5123-6 and 5123:2-6 of the Administrative Code.
An operator will comply with the requirements for reporting medication/treatment errors in accordance with rules 5123-6-07 and 5123-17-02 of the Administrative Code.

An operator shall develop and implement written procedures for the disposal of prescribed medication which require: (a) disposal of prescribed medication to be verified and recorded by two staff members or by an independent external entity; (b) dangerous drugs to be disposed in accordance with rule 4729-9-06 of the Administrative Code.

In the event of termination of services pursuant to rule 5123-3-05, an operator shall ensure: (a) a written accounting of prescribed medication is completed no later than the last day of residency and verified by two staff members; (b) a plan is developed for transfer of prescribed medication to the individual or guardian.

In the event of the death of an individual, an operator shall ensure: (a) a written accounting of prescribed medication is completed immediately and no later than twenty-four hours following the death and verified by two staff members; (b) the operator and staff cooperate with any investigation by a legally authorized entity; (c) disposal of prescribed medication occurs in accordance with the written procedures in (E)(5), unless an investigation calls for the disposal to be delayed.

Transportation - an operator shall: (1) provide or arrange for transportation in accordance with each resident's individual service plan; (2) ensure each employee providing transportation holds a valid driver's license; (3) ensure each such employee is covered by valid personal or corporate liability insurance as specified in Ohio law; (4) obtain a BMV driving record for each such employee no earlier than fourteen calendar days before initial employment as a driver and at least once every three years thereafter (six or more points prohibits providing transportation); (5) require each such employee to immediately notify the operator in writing if the employee accumulates six or more points or the license is suspended or revoked.
Develop and implement written policies and procedures regarding vehicle accessibility, vehicle maintenance, and requirements for vehicle drivers.
An operator shall offer daily meals and snacks that meet an individual's nutritional needs and preferences as identified by the individual.

Modified texture or therapeutic diets shall be prepared and served in accordance with the instructions of a physician or licensed dietitian. An operator shall maintain instructions regarding modified texture or therapeutic diets in accordance with paragraph (J).

Meals shall provide for variety, substitutions, and accommodation of individuals' personal preferences and religious beliefs. Individuals shall participate in meal planning and preparation to the extent of their interest and ability.
Fresh food supplies sufficient for three days and staple food supplies sufficient for at least five days shall be available in the residential facility at all times.

Food shall be prepared and stored properly and in accordance with health codes to protect it against contamination and spoilage. Food products shall be stored separately from potentially harmful non-food items, particularly cleaning and laundry compounds.

Clothing - an operator shall ensure each individual has an adequate amount of personal clothing in good repair, well-fitting, and comparable in style to that worn by age peers in the community (the team ensures needs are met for an individual without personal funds), and shall encourage each individual to select, purchase, and maintain own clothing and to dress as independently as possible.

When an individual has been assessed to need assistance with management of personal possessions, the operator shall record the individual's clothing and personal belongings within fourteen calendar days of admission and update the record at least annually. Any single item with a purchase price of fifty dollars or more shall be added to the record when acquired and deleted when discarded or lost.

An operator shall not discard an individual's clothing or personal belongings without the consent of the individual or guardian. If operation is transferred to another operator, the outgoing operator shall convey individuals' clothing and personal belongings to the incoming operator.

Current records for each individual maintained at the residential facility: (i) a photograph; (ii) legal status; (iii) individual service plan, including documentation of informed consent; (iv) signed authorization to seek medical treatment or documentation that attempts to secure it were unsuccessful; (v) medication and/or treatment records showing the prescriber and the date, time, and person who administered.

Records maintained in an accessible location and provided on request to the department: (i) former versions of (J)(1)(a) records; (ii) admission and referral records; (iii) all service documentation including notations of progress; (iv) medical and dental examination and immunization records; (v) records of major unusual incidents and unusual incidents; (vi) major unusual incident investigation files; (vii) reconciliations of the individual's account transaction record (rule 5123-2-07); (viii) records of negotiable items owned by the individual; (ix) records of clothing and personal belongings; (x) a written accounting within thirty calendar days following termination of residency covering circumstances of termination, new address, conveyance of records/ID/prescriptions/medications, disposition of clothing and belongings, and release or disposition of personal funds.
If operation of a residential facility is transferred from one operator to another, the outgoing operator shall convey the records specified in paragraph (J)(1) to the incoming operator.

All information contained in an individual's records shall be considered confidential. Records will be maintained in accordance with state and federal regulations and in such a manner to ensure their confidentiality and protect them from unauthorized disclosure.
An operator shall develop a records retention schedule for all records in accordance with applicable state and federal requirements.

Transfer and termination of services policies: an operator will allow each resident to remain in the residential facility and shall not initiate a transfer or termination of services unless: (a) necessary for the resident's welfare and needs can no longer be met without undue hardship on the operation; (b) the resident no longer needs or wants the services or chooses to move; (c) the resident is creating a significant risk of substantial harm to self, other residents, or staff; (d) nonpayment for the stay, including nonpayment of medicaid or other third-party payer; (e) the facility permanently reduces its capacity; or (f) the facility ceases to operate.

An operator shall not unlawfully discriminate because of disability, race, color, religion, national origin or ancestry, sex, or age, including failing to make reasonable accommodation to a person's physical, mental, or behavioral support needs to the extent required by law unless the accommodation would impose an undue hardship.

Before initiating a transfer or termination of services, an operator shall: (a) notify the individual and the county board in writing via certified mail, with notice containing (i) the reason, (ii) the effective date, (iii) a summary of action taken by the operator, including working with the county board, to try to meet the resident's needs, (iv) the individual's right to appeal and the process, and (v) the telephone number and address of disability rights Ohio; (b) explain the transfer or termination and appeal rights in a manner the individual understands; and (c) record the reasons in the resident's record.

Notice must be made at least thirty calendar days before the transfer or termination, except when an emergency exists (the individual may return if the emergency conditions no longer exist before the thirty days expire). If the individual requests a hearing, the facility must maintain services or the availability of services until a decision is rendered unless an emergency exists. If the individual waives appeal rights in writing, the operator is not required to maintain services.

Administrative review process: the individual first appeals in writing to the governing board or administrator within seven calendar days of receipt of the notice; the governing board or administrator notifies the individual in writing of the outcome within five calendar days (by certified mail, with director contact information and explanation if denied); the individual then has five calendar days from receipt to appeal in writing to the director.

Mediation process: the individual and the operator shall attend a mediation meeting before the hearing process (legal representation not permitted); the department provides the mediator; the meeting is held within fifteen calendar days of receipt of the appeal; mediation is nonbinding unless all parties agree in writing; statements made in mediation cannot be used as evidence in later hearings or court proceedings.

Hearing process: the department grants a hearing to an individual who received a notice, attended mediation, and requests a hearing; the hearing officer (not the mediator) is appointed by the department; the hearing is held within thirty calendar days of the end of mediation; the burden of proof is on the operator; the hearing officer issues a written recommendation within ten calendar days; the director issues a written decision within five calendar days and may impose conditions.
If an operator fails to follow the requirements of this rule or fails to follow the decision of the director, the operator may be subject to adverse actions in accordance with rule 5123-3-06.

official.notes: No single DODD policy-review checklist or form (like Maryland's DD.APP.1.1 or California's LIC 281) was found for Ohio residential facility licensure. The items above come from the regulation sections that list required written policies and plans, as the instructions allow. Only 5123-3-01(C)(5)(b), (D)(7) and (E)(5) of 5123-3-04, (F)(6) of 5123-3-04, (F)(1) of 5123-3-02 and (C) of 5123-3-05 use explicit 'written policies/procedures/plan' wording. The other items are practice requirements that a facility's manual should address. Ohio has no prescribed manual order, so the sections above follow the rules' own paragraph order. Under ORC 5123.19, the applicant applies to the DODD Director. The Director conducts a pre-license survey, and DODD then reviews compliance (OAC 5123-3-06). That rule says a compliance review includes an examination of the facility's policies, and an abbreviated review focuses on background checks, behavioral support, medication administration, major unusual incidents and service delivery. The 5123-3-01 appendices A-D (training topics for administrators, DSPs, support staff and volunteers) set the content of the required training plan (D)(7)(a). They are linked from the rule page and were not read here. Fire safety and emergency plan: the rule requires approval by the state/local authority (fire marshal/local fire department, or Red Cross/county EMA) and sharing the plan with the county board. Related rules that apply but were not reviewed in this pass: 5123-2-02 (background checks), 5123-2-06 (behavioral support/restrictive measures), 5123-2-07 (individual funds), 5123-17-02 (incident reporting) and 5123-6 (medication). Person-centered planning (5123-3-03, effective 8/27/2026) puts assessment and the ISP with the county board's SSA for non-ICF/IID facilities. Its detailed ISP steps apply to ICF/IIDs and are omitted. For HCBS/IO waiver services (Homemaker/Personal Care under 5123-9-30; Shared Living under 5123-9-33), 5123-3-01(C)(3) requires a separate HCBS approval application, an ODM Medicaid provider agreement, and compliance with Chapter 5123-9. Those rules' service-specific requirements were not reviewed here. Verify them separately on codes.ohio.gov. The 5123-3-04 text was read from Cornell LII, so confirm it against the codes.ohio.gov version before submitting.
